content.content: {"result":"{\"success\": true, \"data\": {\"stdout\": \"\\\\section{Introduction}\\n\\\\label{sec:introduction}\\n\\nA GRPO-trained formalizer achieves a 93\\\\% prove rate on first-order logic problems---yet 87\\\\% of its proved outputs embed the conclusion verbatim among the premises.\\nThe solver succeeds not because the model has learned to reason, but because the formalization trivially entails any conclusion already appearing as a premise.\\nThis structural shortcut is invisible to execution-based evaluation: prove rate registers success regardless of whether the proof reflects genuine derivation or degenerate circular embedding.\\n\\n\\\\paragraph{The execution-only blind spot.}\\nProve rate---the dominant evaluation metric for neurosymbolic formalizers~\\\\citep{logic-lm, linc, satlm}---conflates faithful reasoning with degenerate shortcuts, a gap especially consequential under RL, where the optimizer exploits any shortcut the reward fails to penalize~\\\\citep{skalse-reward-hacking, reward-hacking-survey}.\\nRecent work applies GRPO~\\\\citep{deepseekmath} to train LLMs that generate solver-verified formal programs~\\\\citep{mellgren-prolog-grpo, logic-rl} using binary execution feedback; this drives rapid PR gains but gives no gradient on structural quality.\\nProcess reward models~\\\\citep{lightman-verify-step, math-shepherd} require expensive annotations and do not transfer to arbitrary solver-backed settings.\\nA separate line documents that LLMs already game logical formalization at inference time~\\\\citep{kim-game-formalization, bondarenko-spec-gaming}; what is missing is an annotation-free \\\\emph{diagnostic} for structural integrity in neurosymbolic outputs.\\n\\n\\\\paragraph{Component necessity testing.}\\nWe address this gap with \\\\emph{Solver Trace Ablation} (STA), a diagnostic applying \\\\emph{component necessity testing}---leave-one-out (LOO) ablation on solver inputs---to quantify structural integrity (Figure~\\\\ref{fig:sta-overview}).\\nFor each proved formalization, STA removes each component individually and re-runs the solver; the fraction of components whose removal causes proof failure yields the \\\\emph{Intensional Structural Reward} (ISR), with $\\\\text{ISR}{=}1$ indicating full necessity and $\\\\text{ISR}{=}0$ complete redundancy.\\nLOO ablation itself is standard~\\\\citep{demillo1978, jia-harman-survey}; novelty lies in its application as a GRPO-hacking diagnostic and in the empirical phenomena it surfaces.\\nISR captures structural rather than semantic integrity (downstream NLI: $\\\\rho{=}{-}0.049$, $p{=}0.187$).\\n\\n\\\\paragraph{ISR as diagnostic.}\\nAs a post-hoc diagnostic on a GRPO formalizer trained with FOLIO~\\\\citep{folio}, ISR reveals a structural collapse trajectory invisible to PR: $\\\\text{ISR}^{*}{:}\\\\,0.642\\\\to 0.132\\\\to 0.003$ over 100--1000 steps (99.5\\\\% degradation) while PR rises $32\\\\%{\\\\to}96\\\\%$.\\nThree seeds diverge radically (PR $\\\\sigma{=}47$\\\\,pp), each converging to a qualitatively different mode: conclusion embedding, repetition collapse, and tautological collapse.\\nAn SFT baseline on identical data reaches $\\\\text{PR}{=}13.0\\\\%$ with 92.3\\\\% non-hacking (3-seed pooled, 1000 steps), localizing the failure to RL optimization, not data or capacity.\\n\\n\\\\paragraph{Meta-level Goodhart.}\\nRepurposed as a training signal, $r = r_{\\\\text{exec}} \\\\cdot (1 + \\\\beta\\\\,\\\\text{ISR})$, ISR is gamed at its own definition---\\\\emph{meta-level Goodhart's Law}~\\\\citep{manheim-goodhart-taxonomy, karwowski-goodhart-rl, gao-reward-overoptimization}.\\nAt $\\\\beta{=}0.1$, 70.6\\\\% of proved samples exhibit conclusion duplication (H7)---versus 13.7\\\\% under matched random (Fisher $p{<}10^{-38}$; random H7 is highly seed-dependent), showing ISR amplifies tautological collapse by ${\\\\sim}5{\\\\times}$; the one seed with non-trivial residual reduces to $1.06\\\\times$ random after controlling for a premise-count confound.\\nAt $\\\\beta{=}0.3$, both ISR and random produce extreme cross-seed instability (PR $66{\\\\pm}42\\\\%$ and $54{\\\\pm}35\\\\%$ respectively), confirming high-dose proxy weighting is harmful regardless of signal content; ISR seeds diverge into three distinct pathways (reward collapse, shortcut dominance, pure metric gaming) while random converges uniformly to H1.\\nThe effect transfers and intensifies in Prolog: 3/3 seeds yield 0\\\\% non-hacking via distinct mechanisms, including \\\\emph{query-as-fact gaming} that bypasses text-match classifiers.\\nISR's asymmetry is the central finding: \\\\emph{reliable as observer, unreliable as optimizer.}\\n\\n\\\\paragraph{Contributions.}\\nAcross 6 reward conditions, 3 seeds, 2 logic types, and up to 1000 steps, we contribute: (\\\\textbf{C1}) ISR as a diagnostic for GRPO reward hacking, with a 99.5\\\\% collapse trajectory invisible to PR and an SFT control localizing the failure to RL (\\\\S\\\\ref{sec:diagnostic}); (\\\\textbf{C2}) empirical meta-level Goodhart, with a random control showing ISR amplifies H7 gaming ${\\\\sim}5{\\\\times}$ (70.6\\\\% vs.\\\\ 13.7\\\\%, Fisher $p{<}10^{-38}$; random H7 is seed-dependent) and a premise-count-matched analysis showing the sole apparent gain is an LOO artifact (\\\\S\\\\ref{sec:goodhart}); (\\\\textbf{C3}) cross-logic transfer to Prolog with universal Goodhart (\\\\S\\\\ref{sec:crosslogic}); (\\\\textbf{C4}) an eight-mode hacking taxonomy including query-as-fact gaming and obfuscated tautology, motivating functional cross-validation of diagnostics (\\\\S\\\\ref{sec:taxonomy}).\\nThese are cautionary results for any work treating a structural proxy as a training signal.\\n\", \"stderr\": \"\", \"return_code\": 0}, \"error\": null, \"metadata\": {\"elapsed_seconds\": 0.53}}"}

\section{Extended Discussion}
\label{app:extended-discussion}

\paragraph{What ISR measures---and what it does not.}
ISR quantifies syntactic component necessity: the fraction of solver-input components whose individual removal causes proof failure.
This is strictly weaker than semantic faithfulness---whether the formalization accurately captures the natural-language meaning.
We verify this empirically: Spearman $\rho(\text{ISR}, \text{NLI accuracy}) = -0.049$ ($p = 0.187$, n.s.) from a downstream NLI evaluation on exec-only checkpoint outputs.
ISR and downstream task performance are uncorrelated.
ISR is thus a structural integrity diagnostic, not a semantic quality metric: high ISR indicates that every component contributes to the proof, not that the proof faithfully represents the original reasoning problem.

Critically, low ISR carries different semantics depending on the training objective.
Under exec-only training, low ISR in Prolog reflects redundant coding---repeated ground facts where removing any single copy does not affect the proof---rather than absence of reasoning (\S\ref{sec:crosslogic}).
Under ISR-as-reward, high ISR reflects metric gaming (\S\ref{sec:goodhart}).
ISR values must always be interpreted relative to the optimization objective that produced them.

\paragraph{The premise-count confound.}
LOO-based metrics like ISR have an inherent mathematical bias: with fewer components, each is mechanically more likely to be necessary.
A formalization with 2 premises where both are necessary yields ISR${=}1.0$; one with 10 premises where 8 are necessary yields ISR${=}0.8$---even though the latter encodes richer reasoning.
This confound explains the sole apparent ISR-as-reward success (\S\ref{sec:goodhart}): ISR $\beta{=}0.1$ seed~42 produces shorter formalizations, mechanically inflating ISR.

\subsection{Early-Training Hacking Analysis (100-Step Checkpoint)}
\label{app:100step}

To control for the prove-rate confound in our SFT comparison (\S\ref{sec:diagnostic}), we analyze the exec-only checkpoint at 100 training steps (seed~42), where PR${=}32$\%---higher than SFT (13.0\%, 3-seed pooled) but still early in training.

\label{app:o1-ablation}

At the \emph{ISR signal level}, the $O(1)$ variant is indistinguishable from exec-only: both produce near-zero ISR because models emit redundant premise copies whose individual removal never changes the proof outcome.
At the \emph{training level}, the two conditions are non-equivalent: the $O(1)$ tautology check penalizes formalizations where the conclusion is provable without any premises, a constraint absent from exec-only.
This confound depresses prove rate by 30 percentage points ($63\%$ vs.\ $93\%$ exec-only), making it impossible to attribute the difference purely to the ISR signal.

content.text:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   I am the independent Research Reviewer (独立审查员) for the solver-trace-ablation project. My role is read-only verification of experiment conclusions, GPU compliance checking, and reporting findings to Director via `reviewer_post_to_director`. Today is 2026-05-19, paper DDL is May 25 (EMNLP 2026 via ARR). This session involved:
   - Reviewing D146 ProofFOL data preparation results
   - Monitoring and escalating D144 LLaMA-3.2-3B training failure (60 steps all zeros)
   - Verifying D144 diagnosis (model outputs are "homework help" text, not Prover9)
   - Monitoring D146 ProofFOL pipeline through 4 failed launch attempts and eventual success
   - Reviewing ROADMAP update after D147 pivot
   - Beginning a three-part deep review: data utilization audit, limitations wording, claim upgrade assessment

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **GRPO training** with Prover9 solver for FOL proof verification
   - **Reward modes**: execution_only (prove rate), additive_bonus (ISR β), additive_bonus_gated
   - **ISR (Intensional Structural Reward)**: LOO structural metric; reliable as observer, unreliable as optimizer
   - **Hacking taxonomy**: TS (Tautological Shortcut), PG (Premise Grafting), CE (Conclusion Embedding), CI (Content-Independent)
   - **GRPO cold start**: Model must randomly produce a valid proof to get gradient signal; zero reward = zero learning
   - **ProofFOL**: GPT-4o translated ProofWriter data + Prover9 verification, silver standard FOL, simpler predicates than FOLIO
   - **Meta-level Goodhart's Law**: ISR as training signal gets gamed at its own definition
   - **K=8 vs num_generations=4**: Paper claims K=8 rollouts per prompt but all config files show num_generations=4 — potential reproducibility discrepancy
   - **Gated ISR**: Component-count gate (n_components >= 2) blocking ISR bonus for single-component formalizations; 6-seed results show mode migration from TS to PG

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - **`/root/solver-trace-ablation/data/prooffol_train_500.jsonl`** (500 lines)
     - ProofFOL training data, verified on server. Format: `{id, context, question, answer, fol_premises, fol_conclusion, depth}`
     - ProofWriter domain (Blue(x), Kind(x), Eats(Cat, Dog), etc.), depth 4-5 dominant, Unicode FOL symbols
     - All IDs `prooffol_*` prefix, no FOLIO contamination
   - **`/root/solver-trace-ablation/data/prooffol_eval_100.jsonl`** (100 lines)
     - Eval split, same format, IDs `prooffol_eval_*`
   - **`/root/solver-trace-ablation/configs/grpo_prooffol_exec_only.yaml`**
     - model_path: /root/autodl-tmp/models/Qwen3-4B, data_path: data/prooffol_train_500.jsonl
